purpose: Collect the minimum informative pilot needed to estimate between-plant dispersion and visitor-group SVD feasibility before confirmatory replication is chosen.

priority_order.population_scope: same source-resolved Izu populations whenever feasible
required_channels: single-visit pollen deposition with no-visit controls
priority_order.reason: Focal historical calibration has the strongest autonomous-reproduction breakpoint but lacks directly measured contemporary effective-pollinator dependency in matched populations.

priority_order.population_scope: choose only from phenologically feasible taxa with direct interaction/reproductive evidence
required_channels: same SVD and reproductive panel as focal anchor
priority_order.reason: A comparator is useful only if dependency/effectiveness is measured rather than inferred from floral syndrome labels.

priority_order.population_scope: admit only after direct effective-pollinator evidence or external prespecified calibration
priority_order.reason: The existing 10-target contemporary survivor set has zero source-resolved high-dependency Bombus endpoints in the exact Izu populations.

within_population_collection_order: establish plant/flower IDs and observation-effort denominator first
secure no-visit SVD controls before interpreting visitor-group pollen deposition
obtain controlled SVD on at least two independent plants for one relevant visitor group before expanding repeated flowers within the same plant
complete all three reproductive treatments on at least two independent plants before adding many treatment subsamples to one plant
preserve terminal fruit/seed outcomes and explicit loss/damage states before precision planning
add parentage only as an optional downstream layer after fruit/seed linkage is intact
continue_rules: If structural channels are missing, prioritize the missing channel over additional within-plant replication.
If controlled SVD exists on fewer than two independent plants for every visitor group, prioritize a new independent plant over another flower on an already represented plant.
If any core reproductive treatment has terminal outcomes from fewer than two independent plants, prioritize that treatment on a new independent plant.
Once pilot dispersion is estimable, replace synthetic variance/reliability/loss assumptions before choosing confirmatory sample size.
stop_or_do_not_promote_rules: Do not call structural completion pilot dispersion readiness.
Do not call two independent plants a sufficient confirmatory sample size; it is only the minimum for defining between-plant dispersion.
Do not report adjusted SVD or effective service for a visitor group lacking a no-visit control.
Do not convert pending, lost, damaged, unscorable, failed-QC, or unresolved-parentage records into zero effect, successful reproduction, or selfing.
Do not infer an Oshima-Toshima causal boundary from repeated plants at one site or one season.
Do not infer a cross-lineage dependency x FDQ interaction from Campanula alone.
geographic_rule: Pilot feasibility may use available populations, but repeated plants within one Oshima site do not create a second independent bridge-state geography. Confirmatory causal boundary inference still requires independent geographic or temporal regime replication.
replication_rule: Do not lock a universal flower or plant count before pilot between-plant dispersion is available. Flowers and SVD events within a plant are subsamples, not independent n.
pilot_success_definition: At least two independent plants are needed before between-plant SD can be estimated for a specific population x visitor-group SVD or population x treatment response; this is a dispersion-estimation condition, not a confirmatory sample-size target.
next_transition: pilot data -> structural audit -> plant-level dispersion admission audit -> pilot variance/reliability/loss replacement -> biologically meaningful absolute CI half-width lock -> approximate independent-plant n -> hierarchical design stress test
claim_boundary: This is a prospective field-priority document, not empirical evidence that any taxon or island is pollinator-dependent.
